newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-NYLANDER LEADS SWEDEN, KOIVU FINLAND TO WINS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-NYLANDER LEADS SWEDEN, KOIVU FINLAND TO WINS.

text.p: Michael Nylander scored one goal and set up another as Sweden maintained their 100 percent record at the ice hockey world championship with a 4-1 win over Norway in group B on Tuesday.
In group A in Helsinki, Finland kept alive their hopes of playing in the final with an easy 6-0 win against Germany.
Sweden's victory left them at the top of their group with six points. Norway have lost their opening three matches.
Finland lead group A with four points but still have to play Russia and Slovakia.
Like Norway, Germany have lost their three opening games and both squads look certain to travel to Tampere for the relegation play-offs next week after the peliminary round-robin group games.
Sweden dominated the opening period but fell behind when Matts Trygg intercepted a long clearing pass at the blue line and blasted a low slapshot past surprised netminder Johan Hedberg.
But in the second period the Swedes moved ahead 2-1, wearing down the tired Norwegians who had gone down 3-1 to the United States 24 hours earlier.
Defenceman Marcus Ragnarsson levelled the scores when his low slap shot from the point found its way past unsighted netminder Robert Schistad.
Nylander, who is expected to join the NHL's Calgary Flames next season, set up the second for Per Eklund with a dazzling move that left a trio of Norwegian defenders looking on in amazement.
Nylander sealed Norway's fate just 17 seconds into the final period when he stole the puck from Jan-Roar Fagerli then broke in alone on Schistad.
Finland's game against a worn-out Germany resembled 60 minutes of power-play. On Monday, Russia beat the Germans 5-1.
Montreal Canadiens attacker Saku Koivu opened the scoring just 70 seconds into his first game of the tournament, circling from behind the German goal before whipping in a low backhand shot.
Defender Mika Stromberg hit the net twice and set up a third goal for the Finns, who kept up a relentless offensive pressure and scored twice in each period.
Finnish goalkeeper Jarmo Myllys hardly broke into a sweat while German colleague Olaf Kolzig of the Washington Capitals made 47 saves.
After Sunday's loss against titleholders the Czech Republic the win was important for the Finnish side, whose coach Curt Lindstrom still has his eyes set firmly on the final.
"We can still see our goal. As long as we can see our goal we can work towards it. Our goal is to play in the final," he said.
